$comment: Golden vectors for docs/BLOB_HTTP_SURFACE.md 'Blob URL resolution (optional capability)' section (slice S4.1): GET /blobs/{hash}/url and POST /blobs/{hash}/uploaded. Unlike the relay-surface vectors (blob-http-surface-vectors.v1.json), the expected response depends on whether the server has a presign-capable backend behind IBlobUrlResolverProvider / BlobPersistence's resolve_get_url/resolve_put_url hooks, not on stored bytes — so each vector carries a `backend_configured` flag instead of `seeded`. When backend_configured is true, harnesses wire in a fake resolver that returns `fake_presigned_url` with `fake_ttl_seconds`; when false, harnesses wire in one that always returns null (or omit registration entirely) to model 'no delegated backend'. Consumed by: hosts/dotnet/tests/NodalMerge.DotNetHost.Tests/BlobUrlResolutionVectorTests.cs (.NET, implemented in S4.1). The Rust server has no HTTP implementation of this section yet (that's slice 4.2, per docs/BLOB_STORAGE_LAYOUT.md's Phase 4 plan) — this file exists now so 4.2's harness can pick it up without a parallel vector-authoring pass. If you change the surface, this file, the .NET harness, the future Rust harness, and docs/BLOB_HTTP_SURFACE.md must move together.

vectors.description: GET op=get against a server with a presign-capable backend -> 200 {url, expiresAtUtc}

GET op=put with size/contentType against a server with a presign-capable backend -> 200 {url, expiresAtUtc}; size/contentType flow to the presign delegate as metadata (docs/BLOB_STORAGE_LAYOUT.md §7), not asserted here since they never affect key derivation or the response shape
GET op=get against a server with no presign-capable backend -> 501 (relay-only deployments stay conformant with zero change)
GET op=put against a server with no presign-capable backend -> 501
malformed hash -> 400, same rule as GET/HEAD/PUT /blobs/{hash}; checked before the backend/op is consulted
op=put without a positive size is malformed

upload confirmation with a resolver registered -> 200; the .NET host has no bucket visibility today so it MAY-accepts without verification (docs/delegated-storage-gc.md Uploading -> Active), mirroring the Rust delegate auth mode's verify_uploaded default of Ok(())
upload confirmation with no resolver registered at all -> 501
malformed hash -> 400, checked before the backend is consulted
